title: News & Events
intro: Announcements, results, admissions updates, and stories from the LIS community in Kisakasaka, Zanzibar.

items.title: Admissions Open for All Classes — Interviews Ongoing (Cambridge & NECTA Curriculums)
items.excerpt: Applications and interviews are now ongoing across Baby Class, Nursery (KG1 & KG2), NECTA Grades 1–6, and Cambridge Years 1–6.
items.imageAlt: Leaders International School Admissions Open All Classes Poster

body.text: Leaders International School has published the official 2026/2027 Fee Structure and opened admissions for the January 2027 intake across both our NECTA National Wing and our Cambridge Assessment International Education Wing.

items: Baby Class — TZS 3,200,000 per annum (TZS 266,667 per month).
Nursery (KG1 & KG2) — TZS 3,500,000 per annum (TZS 291,667 per month).
NECTA Grade 1 – 3 — TZS 3,700,000 per annum (TZS 308,333 per month).
NECTA Grade 4 – 6 — TZS 3,900,000 per annum (TZS 325,000 per month).
Cambridge Year 1 – 3 — TZS 5,400,000 per annum (TZS 450,000 per month).
Cambridge Year 4 – 6 — TZS 7,020,000 per annum (TZS 585,000 per month).

body.text: Every monthly instalment includes tuition, stationery, caution fee, daily school breakfast & lunch, and daily other curriculum. New students pay a one-time registration fee of TZS 100,000 on admission. Download the official PDF under Resources or apply online today.

items.title: We Are Hiring: Cambridge & NECTA Teachers, Accountant, Receptionist & Media/IT
items.excerpt: Join our dedicated team shaping future leaders in Zanzibar. Applications close on 4th December 2026.
items.imageAlt: Leaders International School We Are Hiring poster

body.text: As Leaders International School prepares for the January 2027 intake, we are expanding our teaching faculty and administrative team in Kisakasaka, Zanzibar.

items: Cambridge Wing Teachers — English, Art & Design, Mathematics/Science, Humanities, and PE/Global Perspectives.
Teachers (All Subjects) — Passionate educators with strong communication skills and commitment to student development.
Accountant — Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance or related field; financial reporting, invoicing, reconciliations, and budgeting.
Receptionist — Diploma or certificate in Office Management/Administration; front desk, visitor care, and MS Office proficiency.
Media & IT Officer — Degree or diploma in Media, ICT, or Computer Science; digital content creation, school website management, and IT support.

body.text: Send your academic documents and CV to info@leaderinternationalschool.ac.tz or leadersinternationalerp@gmail.com, or call +255 777 427 140 before 4th December 2026.

items.title: Science Fair 2026 – Inspiring Young Innovators
items.excerpt: Forty-two pupil projects, three district judges, and a first-place district award for our Upper Primary robotics and science team.
items.imageAlt: Pupils presenting a volcano model at the science fair

body.text: Our annual Science & Innovation Fair filled the main hall with forty-two working projects built by our NECTA and Cambridge Primary learners, from a low-cost water purifier built from clay and charcoal to an automated solar garden sensor.

items: Best in Show — "Pumza", a greywater filter for household use, Grade 6.
Best Lower Primary Project — a model volcano with a natural hibiscus pH indicator, Cambridge Year 3.
Best STEM Presentation — our Coding & Robotics club greenhouse controller, Year 6.

body.text: The judges were impressed less by the equipment than by how clearly the children explained their scientific reasoning. That is what we teach for.
body.author: Academic Directorate, Leaders International School

body.text: Thanks to the parents who supplied materials, to the visiting judges, and to our science teachers for two weeks of late afternoons in the laboratory.

items.title: Sports Day Highlights on the Kisakasaka Field
items.excerpt: A day full of energy, teamwork and school spirit — 14 house records broken across Pre-Primary and Primary relays.
items.imageAlt: LIS boys' football team playing on the school field

body.text: Learners from Baby Class right up to Grade 6 and Year 6 competed across sprint relays, football, netball, obstacle courses, and the always-contested parents-versus-teachers tug-of-war. Nakupenda house took the overall shield for the third year running.

items: Boys' 100m (Upper Primary) — new school record, Grade 6.
Girls' 4x100m Relay — Nakupenda house victory.
Nursery obstacle relay — every KG1 and KG2 learner crossed the line with a ribbon.

body.text: Photographs from the day are in the gallery under Sport.

items.title: 640 New Library Titles & Junior Reading Corner
items.excerpt: 640 new titles, a carpeted reading corner for Baby Class to Grade 3, and offline digital encyclopedias.
items.imageAlt: Two pupils choosing books from the new library shelves

body.text: The library has added 640 titles chosen with our English, Kiswahili, and Cambridge Primary teachers: phonics readers for KG1 to Year 3, illustrated science encyclopedias, and East African storybooks.

items: A carpeted reading corner for Lower Primary with 180 picture books.
Two offline encyclopedia workstations in the library.
Daily guided reading timetabled for every class before morning break.

items.title: Annual Graduation & Academic Awards Ceremony
items.excerpt: Celebrating our graduating KG2 and Grade 6 / Year 6 cohorts with parents, awards, and cultural performances.
items.imageAlt: Graduating pupils receiving certificates on stage

body.text: Families gathered on the Kisakasaka campus to celebrate our KG2 pupils stepping up into Grade 1 / Year 1 and our senior primary pupils completing Grade 6 with a 98% pass rate.
We were taught here that a leader is not the person at the front of the queue, it is the person who turns round to make sure nobody is left behind.
body.author: Head Pupil Address
